title: Terraform: set residency region pinning defaults + add guardrails to prevent misconfigured multi-region deployments
creator: Hanae Suzuki
body:
Context
- As part of Hosted Data Residency Enforcement, we’re introducing region pinning (pinned_region / allowed_regions) with deterministic routing and no cross-region fallback unless explicitly allowed and audited.
- Enterprise customers typically provision Hosted/Dedicated via Terraform modules. Today, our modules make it easy to accidentally create a “multi-region” footprint (or leave region unspecified), which then surfaces as runtime RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH errors and/or cross-region side effects.

Problem
- Terraform modules don’t currently:
  1) set safe defaults for enterprise accounts (i.e., pinned to a single region by default)
  2) validate combinations of residency settings (pinned_region vs allowed_regions)
  3) detect common misconfigurations (provider region mismatch, inconsistent module variables, multiple endpoints/regions defined for a single workspace)

Goal
- Update Redwood Terraform modules to make the secure path the easiest path:
  - For enterprise templates and examples, default to pinned_region=<deployment_region> and allowed_regions=[<deployment_region>]
  - Add strong validation to prevent creating deployments that will fail at runtime or violate residency expectations
  - Provide explicit, intentional escape hatches for exception workflows (e.g., temporary cross-region fallback allowed), but don’t make them the default

Non-goals
- Automatically migrating existing customer artifacts across regions (handled elsewhere)
- Covering every bespoke customer module fork; focus on official modules and examples

Scope
1) Modules to update
- redwood-hosted (Hosted API org/project/workspace config scaffolding)
- redwood-dedicated (Dedicated capacity provisioning + org/workspace config)
- shared “residency” submodule or locals (if we decide to factor validations)

2) New/updated inputs (proposed)
- var.region (string): canonical deployment region used by the module and passed to providers/base URLs
- var.residency_enabled (bool): default true for enterprise examples; default false for non-enterprise templates
- var.pinned_region (string|null): if set, must equal var.region unless var.allow_region_mismatch_for_testing=true
- var.allowed_regions (list(string)): must include pinned_region if pinned_region is set; for strict pinning should be [var.region]
- var.allow_cross_region_fallback (bool): default false; if true, require var.exception_ticket_id
- var.exception_ticket_id (string|null): required when allow_cross_region_fallback=true (to align with GRC exception process)

3) Guardrails/validation rules
- Exactly one of:
  - pinned_region set (recommended) OR
  - allowed_regions set (non-empty) for multi-region allowlist
- If pinned_region is set:
  - allowed_regions must be either empty/null OR contain pinned_region
  - For enterprise module usage, enforce pinned_region == var.region
- If allowed_regions set with >1 entry:
  - require explicit acknowledgment var.multi_region_ack=true
  - show a warning in outputs (best-effort via a documented note; Terraform doesn’t have “warnings” but we can fail unless ack is true)
- Base URL / endpoint region mismatch guard:
  - If module accepts api_base_url, validate that it corresponds to var.region (best-effort regex check) OR require an explicit var.custom_endpoint_ack=true
- Prevent “accidental dual endpoints”:
  - If both primary and secondary endpoints are configured, require allow_cross_region_fallback=true and exception_ticket_id set

4) Outputs
- Output the effective residency configuration:
  - residency_enabled
  - pinned_region
  - allowed_regions
  - allow_cross_region_fallback
- Output a "residency_troubleshooting" string that links to internal/public docs (once docs PR lands) and lists the configured region(s)

Acceptance criteria
- Enterprise example(s) result in:
  - pinned_region == var.region
  - allowed_regions == [var.region]
  - allow_cross_region_fallback == false
- Terraform plan/apply fails fast with clear error messages for:
  - pinned_region set but not in allowed_regions
  - allowed_regions empty list
  - pinned_region != var.region (enterprise path)
  - multi-region allowlist without explicit ack
  - cross-region fallback enabled without exception_ticket_id
- Documentation updates in module README:
  - explain residency settings
  - common mistakes + how they map to runtime errors (RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH, RESIDENCY_POLICY_DENY)
  - how to request a temporary exception (link to exception process)

Implementation notes
- Use variable validation blocks for simple constraints.
- For conditional validation that depends on multiple variables, prefer local values + precondition blocks on a null_resource or a small "validation" resource pattern (Terraform >= 1.2 preconditions).
- Keep error messages actionable and consistent with our platform terminology (pinned_region, allowed_regions).
- Coordinate naming with control-plane API fields (ENG-2841) so module inputs map 1:1 to API payload.

Rollout plan
- Phase 1: Land changes behind a module major/minor version bump (depending on breaking changes).
- Phase 2: Update enterprise templates/examples used by Solutions Eng + Sales.
- Phase 3: Notify internal teams (Support/CS) of new validations and expected customer questions.

Risks / open questions
- Backwards compatibility: customers may already be using allowed_regions in ways that become invalid. Need to decide whether to:
  - keep permissive behavior for existing variables (soft deprecation), or
  - enforce strict validation and require updates.
- Provider region vs product region: some customers deploy infrastructure in one cloud region but call a different Redwood region endpoint. We should support this only with explicit acknowledgment and clear documentation.

References / links
- Linear initiative: PM-482 Hosted Data Residency Enforcement
- Related eng tickets: ENG-2841 (policy storage/model), ENG-2842 (gateway enforcement), ENG-2843 (routing fallback)
- Terraform PR to be created in redwood-terraform repo (track under this ticket)
comments: 2026-01-14 — Hanae Suzuki: For enterprise packaging, we should default to strict pinning. I’d like the module to *fail* if someone sets multiple allowed_regions without an explicit ack. This has been a recurring source of confusion in security reviews.

2026-01-21 — Bruno Silva: Drafted validations using Terraform preconditions (Terraform >=1.2). One question: should we enforce pinned_region==region only when var.enterprise=true, or always? I’m leaning enterprise-only to avoid breaking dev/test patterns.

2026-01-23 — Marcus Lin: +1 enterprise-only enforcement, but require explicit allow_region_mismatch_for_testing for non-enterprise. Also, please add exception_ticket_id requirement when allow_cross_region_fallback=true to align with the exception process and audit evidence.

2026-02-04 — Rafael Mendes: Please ensure error messages are copy/pastable into Support responses. We saw customers stuck on RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH; Terraform should stop them earlier with a clear “Your pinned_region=eu-west but api_base_url points to us-east” message if possible.

2026-02-10 — Bruno Silva: Implemented best-effort api_base_url check (regex for ".eu-" / "eu" token) with custom_endpoint_ack override. Added multi_region_ack requirement when allowed_regions has >1 entry. Need final naming alignment with ENG-2841 before merge.

2026-02-18 — Benji Okafor: Naming from ENG-2841 is pinned_region + allowed_regions (exactly). Please keep module inputs consistent. For API payload, we will accept null pinned_region with allowed_regions only. Recommend module enforces either pinned_region or allowed_regions non-empty.

2026-02-22 — Bruno Silva: Opened redwood-terraform PR with changes + updated EU-only enterprise example. Marking this In Review; requesting review from Hanae (secure defaults) and Marcus (exception requirements).
